title: Safety audit decisions: strong muscle pain, form with missed reps, the bone-loading block
summary: Three safety boundaries change after the Phase 4 Part 4 independent safety review, each chosen by the Product Owner on 25 October 2026. SAF-003: muscle pain (a burn or soreness) rated 7/10 or more stops that exercise for today; it was always 'carry on'. PROG-008: a form answer other than 'yes' no longer stops the PROG-004 reduction when the reps fell short or the sets were much harder than planned; the easier version is offered only when the library has one. CON-004: the osteoporosis bone-loading block starts with heel drops for its first 4 weeks; small hops follow only for someone who is not a beginner, is under 65 and has reported no hip, knee or ankle pain in the last 4 weeks; the block stays when another condition sets impact 'as tolerated' (controlled high blood pressure). The health-condition table's entries don't change.
safety_review: Phase 4 Part 4 independent safety review (19-25 Oct 2026), findings 3 (small hops from the first session for a 71-year-old beginner with osteoporosis), 8 (muscle pain 9/10 never stops anything), 10 (no bone-loading block with controlled high blood pressure) and 13 (form not solid with missed reps keeps the weight). Each option was put to the Product Owner with the reviewer's cautious-coach view as the recommendation; the implementation is re-checked by an independent reviewer before the Phase 4 gate.

changed_rules.reason: A safety boundary is added: very strong muscle pain was always 'carry on' (Part 4 review finding 8). Chosen by the Product Owner on 25 Oct 2026 (D-121).
changed_rules.statement: Pain is a separate gate from readiness. Joint/tendon pain <=3/10 not worsening: continue with load -10-20% or shorter range. 4-6/10 or worsening: stop the exercise, offer substitutes with joint stress <=1 for that joint, region to conservative mode. >=7/10 or sharp, swelling, instability, locking, numbness/tingling, or after a fall: stop loading the region, end session if whole-body movement affected, suggest a professional. Muscle pain (a burn or soreness) >=7/10: stop that exercise for today and offer other exercises; the region is not put in conservative mode.
changed_rules.uncertainty: Thresholds are expert practice; rehab data (supervised) allow up to 5/10. The 7/10 stop for muscle pain is a cautious-coach choice (Expert Practice), not a studied threshold.

changed_rules.reason: Training direction: a set that missed its reps keeps the same weight when form wasn't solid (Part 4 review finding 13). The Product Owner chose the PROG-004 reduction with the form tip on 25 Oct 2026 (D-121). The offer of an easier version is made only when one exists (review finding 7).
changed_rules.statement: 'Form felt solid?' yes/unsure/no after main lifts and new exercises; unsure -> hold; no -> hold + cue; when the reps fell short of the range on >=2 sets or the sets were much harder than planned, PROG-004's reduction applies instead of the hold (with the cue after 'no'); two no -> offer the easier version (regression) when the library has one, otherwise hold and point to Replace. Bodyweight and assisted ladders: unsure or no holds the rung and the assistance.
changed_rules.uncertainty: Expert practice; the order of the technique and effort checks is a coaching choice.

changed_rules.reason: A safety boundary changes: the bone-loading block began with small hops from the first session for everyone with osteoporosis, a 71-year-old beginner included (Part 4 review finding 3), and disappeared when controlled high blood pressure was also selected (finding 10). Chosen by the Product Owner on 25 Oct 2026 (D-121).
changed_rules.statement: Low-impact, concentric-dominant modalities first; impact work <=1/week and not the day before heavy legs. A short bone-loading block from the osteoporosis condition entry (≤5 min, ≥50 low-level landings) is not an impact session under this rule. It starts with heel drops for its first 4 weeks; small hops follow only for someone who is not a beginner, is under 65 and has reported no hip, knee or ankle pain in the last 4 weeks. The block stays when another condition sets impact 'as tolerated'; a lower impact level (such as osteoarthritis) still removes it.
changed_rules.uncertainty: The UK consensus (ROS22) advises building impact up gradually; the 4 weeks and the age of 65 are expert practice for this app.
